result.summary: This PR reverts the `noexcept` marking on `SaltedOutpointHasher` (added in #16957) so that libstdc++'s `unordered_map` will cache the outpoint hash code per node again, trading a small memory increase for avoided hash recomputation in `CCoinsMap` operations. The author provides extensive benchmarks showing 2-11% speedups across IBD, reindex-chainstate, and assumeutxo loading, with roughly neutral to slightly higher memory use depending on dbcache size. A focused unit test pins the exception-specification and libstdc++ fast-hash classification contracts. The change is a 2-file, ~21 line diff.
result.problem: The 2019 change to mark the outpoint hasher `noexcept` (#16957) saved about 9% peak memory but cost about 1.6% runtime by forcing libstdc++ to recompute hashes instead of caching them in map nodes; that PR's own reviewers speculated caching could recover the performance. Node operators running IBD, reindex, or assumeutxo with typical dbcache settings feel the resulting slower UTXO cache operations.

result.card: This PR reverts the noexcept marking added in #16957 to SaltedOutpointHasher, restoring libstdc++'s per-node cached hash codes for the UTXO cache (CCoinsMap), trading a small memory cost for measured speedups: the author reports up to 11% faster assumeutxo loading and 2-3% faster IBD/reindex-chainstate across several benchmark runs. A single reviewer (optout21) gave a substantive Concept ACK finding no code issues, but also asked whether a clearer __is_fast_hash-based approach would be preferable and left minor nits, none of which the author has answered. The PR is stale: needs rebase, mergeable_state dirty, and the author has been silent for 137 days, with unanswered review comments since 2026-05-28. It also conflicts with two other open PRs by the same author (#35215) and a third-party PR (#35713). Impact is concentrated in the indexes/UTXO-cache area, where sync and assumeutxo-loading speed are directly user-felt; the change to util/hasher.h itself is narrow in scope for general utils purposes.
